check.header:
Lunar base or pressurized rover: oxygen 30 to 36%, pressure below 85.8 kPa, lunar gravity.

NASA's PSI archive lists 60,866 files (13.47 TB) for 24 combustion investigations (listing of 14 November 2026).

398 of them (104.4 GB, 0.77% of the bytes) carry in their name the NASA identifier or the test number of one of the 26 tests recorded inside these oxygen and pressure ranges: 316 files that are not an archive or a video recording (86.85 MB) and 82 archives and video recordings (104.3 GB).

Two labels that NASA wrote (file name, PSI folder, or the identifier inside a test sheet) name the same test for 336 of them; 47 carry one label; for 15 the labels name different tests (15 files naming FLEX-20 and FLEX-21). The team lists these cases and does not resolve them.

The 26 tests are 17 fuel-droplet tests (FLEX, 71.2 to 72.4 kPa) and 9 gas flames (ACME-CFI-G, 50.7 kPa), all in microgravity.

A file that names a test is not shown to hold what a question needs. The counts are Team RAPID's computation from PSI's file listing and NASA's tables.

The pressure range of this scenario reaches up to 85.8 kPa, above the 70.3 kPa (10.2 psi) of the challenge statement, so that tests set to 0.7 atm are inside it. The 17 tests counted for a need inside its oxygen and pressure ranges were recorded at 71.2 to 72.4 kPa, above 10.2 psi; the 9 tests inside the ranges recorded at 50.7 kPa are not counted for a need.
